title: Group a parallel ledger without reordering a statement

blocks.text: The bank's monthly statements are built from the ledger, which hands its lines over as a stream in posting order. For the large business accounts the month has millions of lines, so the stream is parallel. A customer reads a statement from top to bottom and checks it against their own books, and the statement starts with the account's opening line: its first posting of the month.

items: `statements(...)`: each account's lines, in the order they were posted;

blocks.text: Both must give the same answer for a sequential and for a parallel stream. About two lines in total.
The tests hand the methods parallel streams in which some threads get to later lines first.

cases.says: from a sequential stream, each account's statement lists its lines in posting order, and its opening line is its first posting
from a parallel stream, every account gets a statement with all of its lines, and an opening line
a statement keeps posting order even when a thread handles a later line of the account before an earlier one
the opening line is the first one posted, even when a thread handles a later line of the account first

origin.section: groupingByConcurrent Trades the Order Inside Each Group for One Shared Map

concepts: groupingByConcurrent and toConcurrentMap fill one shared map in the order threads arrive, so groups lose encounter order and a keep-first merge keeps the first to arrive; groupingBy and toMap keep encounter order.
